lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ender de Souza Batista | Lesson 6 -- Can You Repeat That?
lesson.grammar_point: can / can't for ability and for requests (Can you repeat that, please?)

listenings.text: Hello? Ender? Hello? Sorry, I can't hear you very well. Your voice is very low, and the video stops. I think the connection is bad. Can you stop your video, please? Okay... Can you say something now? Yes! Now I can hear you. It is much better. Okay, can we start? First, the new date for the change.

I can only speak English. I can't speak Portuguese, Hindi or Spanish. But on our global calls, there are people from ten countries. So I have a rule: I always speak slowly, and I use short sentences. And I always say: if you can't understand, write in the chat, or ask me to repeat. It is not a problem. A good call is a call that everybody can understand.

extra_audio.text: The global call starts. Raj talks fast, and Ender can't understand the date. Ender asks: Can you repeat that, please? Raj says the date again, more slowly. Now Ender can understand: November 4.

paras: On a global call, there are people from many countries, and there are many accents: American, British, Indian. You can't understand every word, and that is normal. Many native speakers can't understand every word too!

So what can you do? You can ask: "Can you repeat that, please?" You can say: "Can you speak more slowly?" People are usually happy to help. They can't see your face on the call, so they can't know you have a problem. Say it.

Sometimes the problem is the connection. When the connection is bad, you can't hear the other person. Stop your video and close other programs. And when you are not talking, put your microphone on mute.
